series: What if the countries were swapped?
title: What if Son was German?
checked: Son joined Hamburg's academy in August 2008 aged 16 (Wikipedia); scored on his Bundesliga debut at Köln, Oct 2010, aged 18 (JoongAng Daily, Sky Sports). Korea debut 30 Dec 2010 v Syria (Wikipedia). 2015 Asian Cup final: Luongo 45', Son 90+1', Troisi 105', Australia 2-1 aet (Wikipedia, ESPN). Kazan, 27 June 2018: Korea 2-0 Germany; Kim Young-gwon's goal given by VAR in stoppage time; Neuer lost the ball upfield, Ju Se-jong's long ball, Son into the empty net at 90+6; Germany's first ever group-stage exit (Sports Mole, JoongAng Daily, Daily Star). Germany since Dec 2010: World Cup 2014, Confederations Cup 2017 (Wikipedia). 2026: Korea beat Czechia 2-1, lost 1-0 to Mexico and South Africa, out in the group (NST, Ahram). Asian Games 2018 gold left out (under-23). The German-Son goal is clearly imagined. Kits in the game footage are plain. No game footage of the real Kazan goal: the game always has a keeper in goal, and that goal went into an empty net.

lines.text: Son Heung-min learned his football in Germany. So what if he'd been born German?
lines.say: Sohn Hungmin learned his football in Germany. So what if he'd been born German?

lines.text: At sixteen he moved to Hamburg. At eighteen, he scored on his Bundesliga debut.

scene.title: Hamburger SV
scene.sub: Academy at 16 · Bundesliga goal on debut at 18

lines.text: With Korea, he reached the 2015 Asian Cup final. He equalised in stoppage time. Australia won it in extra time.
lines.say: With Korea, he reached the twenty fifteen Asian Cup final. He equalised in stoppage time. Australia won it in extra time.

lines.text: Then came Kazan, 2018. Korea against the world champions, Germany.
lines.say: Then came Kazan, twenty eighteen. Korea against the world champions, Germany.

scene.headline: Germany need a win in Kazan
scene.standfirst: The world champions must beat South Korea to stay in the World Cup. Korea are already almost out.

lines.text: Stoppage time. Korea score. Germany throw everyone forward, even their keeper, Manuel Neuer.
lines.say: Stoppage time. Korea score. Germany throw everyone forward, even their keeper, Manuel Noyer.

scene.note: Germany throw everyone forward, even Neuer

lines.text: Neuer loses the ball. One long pass, and Son rolls it into an empty net.
lines.say: Noyer loses the ball. One long pass, and Sohn rolls it into an empty net.

scene.headline: Son runs the ball into an empty net
scene.standfirst: Neuer is caught upfield. One long ball, a sprint from halfway, and Korea win 2-0. The world champions are out.

lines.text: The champions were out in the group, for the first time ever.
Now Germany, in Son's years. A World Cup in Brazil, and the Confederations Cup three years later.
lines.say: Now Germany, in Sohn's years. A World Cup in Brazil, and the Confederations Cup three years later.

lines.text: And Korea? No senior trophy. This summer, out in the group again.
So in this alternate world, Son plays for Germany.
lines.say: So in this alternate world, Sohn plays for Germany.

lines.text: And in this imagined Kazan, the goal goes the other way.
Two trophies instead of none, including a World Cup.
Korea's captain, or a German world champion? Which would you rather be? Tell me in the comments.
